api.getContext(), api.getApplicationContext(), api.getClassLoader(), api.getAndroid(), and api.getDevice() return real Dolphy Java objects. Commands are available through api.shellExec(), api.rootExec(), api.shizukuExec(), and api.smartExec().
api.getAndroid() provides advertising, GATT client/server, RFCOMM, bonding, and adapter details. api.getDevice() provides BLE scan, hardware capabilities, and system operations.
Wi-Fi scan results, interfaces, DHCP, channels, NSD, sockets, HTTP, and direct access to the Android WifiManager are available. Root and Shizuku unlock the device\'s system networking tools.

hook_screen() adds an overlay, a FAB, or fully replaces the stock screen. hook_action() intercepts named operations and can modify the data, handle, or cancel the action. provide_service() installs a new implementation of a system capability with priority and a stock fallback.
replace swaps the screen, overlay draws a free-form layer on top of it, top and bottom add a Material 3 panel, and fab adds a compact floating action. Route masks support *, e.g. ir_* or other/*.

Performs a quiet connection to devices via the Blue Ducky vulnerability (CVE-2023-45866) — HID without PIN or pairing confirmation dialogs.

Works against vulnerable targets:
• Android 4.2.2 – Android 13 (before 2023/2024 Bluetooth security patches)
• Unpatched Linux BlueZ stacks
• Some early iOS/macOS revisions

On Android 14+ and freshly patched OEMs the host may still require confirmation or reject unauthenticated HID. "Connect" is the normal path with dialogs; "Quiet connect" uses silent Just Works + auto-confirm pairing.
